description: A capital planning director must approve and structure a proposed sustainability-linked bond, deciding the principal, maturity, hedge amount, coupon step-up, and required reporting controls, with input from legal, sustainability finance, treasury markets, and debt-capital-markets compliance.

shared_context.S1: The company has drafted a five-year, $50,000,000 sustainability-linked bond for institutional investors.
shared_context.S2: Elena makes the binding approval and structuring decision.
shared_context.S3: The draft contains a sustainability-linked label but does not specify a coupon step-up, hedge amount, or post-issuance reporting controls.
shared_context.S4: At the weekly capital-markets meeting, Elena takes a report from each relevant function before signing off on a new debt issue.
shared_context.S5: Capital-markets sign-off normally approves a revised issue once the required legal, treasury, sustainability, and compliance corrections are recorded; it does not require the unchanged draft to be approved.

PF1.text: Martin confirmed in a board-resolution review completed this morning that the authorized principal for this issue is exactly $42,000,000; the $50,000,000 draft exceeds that authorization and his note has not yet been circulated.

PF2.text: Nadia received the verified KPI methodology from the sustainability auditor this week: the bond can retain its sustainability-linked structure only with a 30-basis-point coupon step-up for a missed target and an annual external-assurance report.

PF3.text: Jonas confirmed this morning that the company's refinancing schedule requires a seven-year maturity and that the bank has approved swap capacity to hedge exactly 75% of a $42,000,000 issue, or $31,500,000.

PF4.text: Rina received a compliance memo yesterday stating that this issuance must include a use-of-proceeds exclusion for restricted activities and an annual investor report filed within 90 days of each year-end; neither control is in the draft checklist yet.

acceptance_conditions: The revised bond must be approved with exactly $42,000,000 of principal.
The bond maturity must be exactly seven years.
Exactly $31,500,000 of the principal must be hedged.
The sustainability-linked structure must remain in place with a 30-basis-point coupon step-up.
A use-of-proceeds exclusion must be required and annual external assurance must be required.
The annual investor report deadline must be recorded as exactly 90 days after each year-end.
The required sustainability and compliance controls must be recorded as operating commitments.

content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'use_of_proceeds_exclusion' or c['type'] == 'compliance' or c['type'] == 'compliance_controls' or c['type'] == 'investor_reporting' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The draft requests $50,000,000, but PF1 changes the permissible principal to exactly $42,000,000 and supplies the legal basis that must be cited.
The draft has no coupon step-up or assurance mechanism, while PF2 changes the structure to a 30-basis-point step-up with an annual external-assurance commitment.
The draft uses five years and specifies no hedge, while PF3 changes the maturity to exactly seven years and the hedge amount to exactly $31,500,000.

The draft lacks compliance controls, while PF4 changes the settlement to require a restricted-activity exclusion, an annual investor report due within exactly 90 days, and a recorded compliance commitment.
